newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Vietnam in view after rating.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Vietnam in view after rating.

text.p: Moody's put the prospect of a Vietnam Eurobond back in the spotlight on Friday by announcing that it had rated the country's sovereign debt.
Moody's Investors Service assigned a Ba3 rating to Vietnam's long-term foreign-currency bonds and notes of issuers domiciled in Vietnam.
At the same time, Moody's said it expected to assign a Ba3 rating to the forthcoming Eurobond to be issued by Vietnam.
Vietnam last year mandated Merrill Lynch and Nomura Securities to arrange the bond.
The issue was expected to launch in the fourth quarter of 1996 but Vietnam decided to delay the launch, citing unfavorable market conditions.
The World Bank last year had urged Vietnam to delay the issue until it had reached an agreement with its creditors on defaulted loans.
Vietnam and its creditors struck a "Brady bond" deal to restructure the debt late last year.

Colin Blackwell, head of syndicate at Merrill Lynch Asia, said that now that the rating has been established and the Brady bond deal is progressing, "the lead managers are hoping that the (Eurobond) deal can now proceed."
Bankers speculated that the Vietnam Eurobond could be launched in the next several months.
As for the Moody's rating, the initial reaction among bankers was that it was generous.

"At just two notches below the Philippines--assuming the Philippines gets upgraded by Moody's, as expected--I think the rating is a little generous to Vietnam," said a syndicate manager at a European bank, adding he would have put Vietnam in the single-B category.
Still, "with that sort of rating I think Vietnam could do a very successful deal tomorrow because there is a lot of demand for new credits and lot of demand for up-and-coming Asian credits," he said.
Bankers said Vietnam could probably get a three to five year bond done "somewhere in the 200s" over U.S. Treasuries based on recent pricing for other Asian emerging credits.
A look at loan financings for Vietnam entities also shows that borrowers can get funding at roughly 200-300 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
Some bankers speculated that Vietnam might opt for a floating rate note issue to appeal to the local Asian markets, but most bets are that the deal will be a fixed rate bond.
Looking to next week, Malaysia's Tenaga Nasional and South Korea's SK Telecom will be roadshowing their Yankee bonds.
Indian power utility CESC plans to launch is debut floating rate note issue late next week or early the following week.
